headline: 8 killed in 24 hours as dengue death toll hits 289 this year
summary: Over 1,800 new patients were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh in a single day, according to the Directorate General of Health Services.
details: Eight people died from dengue fever across the country in the 24 hours between Tuesday and Wednesday morning, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the total number of deaths from the mosquito-borne illness this year to 289.
In the same 24-hour period, 1,860 new patients were admitted to hospitals for dengue treatment.
So far this year, a total of 92,216 people have been hospitalized for dengue across Bangladesh.
Of those hospitalized, 86,152 patients have recovered and been discharged from the hospital.

headline: 1,140 dead as measles outbreak worsens in Bangladesh
summary: Six more people died in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 1,140 since March 15, according to the DGHS.
details: Six people died from measles or measles-like symptoms in the last 24 hours, according to the latest report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Since March 15, a total of 1,140 people have died, including 104 confirmed measles cases and 1,036 deaths associated with measles symptoms.
In the last 24 hours, 1,280 new cases of measles symptoms were reported nationwide, bringing the total number of symptomatic patients to 229,300 since March 15.
A total of 22,020 people have been confirmed to have measles since mid-March, with 110 new confirmed cases reported in the last 24 hours.
Hospitalizations have been high, with 177,676 people admitted to hospitals since March 15, of whom 170,473 have been discharged.
The highest number of deaths in the last 24 hours occurred in the Dhaka division, where two people died, while two others died in Chattogram and Sylhet divisions.
Public health experts attribute the record infections and deaths to negligence by the interim government regarding vaccination schedules for 2025.

Experts claim that the government failed to provide adequate vaccination and treatment measures when the outbreak began to rise in March, and that a mass vaccination campaign in April left at least 4 million children unvaccinated.
caption:
1,140 deaths and over 229,000 symptomatic cases. The measles outbreak in Bangladesh is reaching critical levels.

Six people died from measles or measles-like symptoms in the last 24 hours, according to the latest report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

Since March 15, a total of 1,140 people have died, including 104 confirmed measles cases and 1,036 deaths associated with measles symptoms.

In the last 24 hours, 1,280 new cases of measles symptoms were reported nationwide, bringing the total number of symptomatic patients to 229,300 since March 15.

A total of 22,020 people have been confirmed to have measles since mid-March, with 110 new confirmed cases reported in the last 24 hours.

Hospitalizations have been high, with 177,676 people admitted to hospitals since March 15, of whom 170,473 have been discharged.

The highest number of deaths in the last 24 hours occurred in the Dhaka division, where two people died, while two others died in Chattogram and Sylhet divisions.

Public health experts attribute the record infections and deaths to negligence by the interim government regarding vaccination schedules for 2025.

Experts claim that the government failed to provide adequate vaccination and treatment measures when the outbreak began to rise in March, and that a mass vaccination campaign in April left at least 4 million children unvaccinated.
